question: How much residual moisture did the water-processed NMC532 cathode lose between 20 °C and drying at 120 °C, and how does its final value compare with the NMP-processed cathode dried at 100 °C?

rendered: The water-processed NMC532 cathode started at 625 ppm[1] of residual moisture at the starting temperature and ended at 47 ppm[2] after drying at the higher temperature, a loss of 578[3] ppm of residual moisture. Its final value is therefore lower than that of the NMP-processed cathode dried under vacuum at the lower temperature, which retained 87 ppm[4], a difference of 40[5] ppm in favour of the water-based cathode. The NMP cathode was dried at a lower temperature, and the water-based cathode reaches its lower value only by raising its drying temperature, which the document describes as albeit at a higher energy consumption[6].
